about: Every name the guide shows to a person comes from this list. Keep the term in English in every conversation language and explain it the first time it appears. `avoid` lists words that must not replace the term in plugin text.

trust.summary: Only a search summary of the source was read.
trust.practice: Widely used in the trade; no single source traced.
trust.unchecked: A named standard recalled from memory; not yet re-read for this list.
trust.coined: Named in this project or by its owner. Not an industry term.

inherited_from: Rows marked inherited carry the trust level recorded in the owner's architecture note of 2026-11-09; they were not re-read for this list.

terms.meaning: The smallest named design decisions: a colour, a spacing step, a type size.
terms.source: W3C Design Tokens Community Group, Technical Reports 2025.10

terms.meaning: Three layers of tokens: primitive (raw values), semantic (roles), component (bound to one component). The token format does not define them; teams choose.
The tier that holds design tokens and the rules for colour, typography, spacing, shape, elevation, motion, iconography and layout.
terms.source: Common practice (Material Design, Atlassian, Primer use it as a top-level section)

terms.meaning: One set of token values for one identity or mode. The structure of the tokens stays the same across themes.
The single colour a whole palette is derived from. Material Design 3 says source color; Flutter's API calls the same thing a seed colour.
terms.source: Material Design 3, How the system works (read 2026-11-11); Flutter, ColorScheme.fromSeed

terms.meaning: The tones of one key colour from black to white that color roles pick from. Tones run from 0 to 100.
terms.source: Material Design 3, How the system works (read 2026-11-11)

terms.meaning: What a colour is for (primary, on-primary, surface, outline), as opposed to which colour it is.
The luminance ratio between text or a control and what is behind it. At level AA: at least 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text, and 3:1 for interface components and graphical objects.
terms.source: WCAG 2.2, Understanding 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) and 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (read 2026-11-11)

terms.meaning: The smallest area a pointer control may offer: at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels at level AA, with exceptions.
The accessibility level a product commits to: A, AA or AAA. Levels add up: AA includes everything in A.
Whether people with disabilities can perceive and operate the product. Measured against a conformance level.
What the product is and who uses it, as far as it changes design decisions.
Whether people work in the screens (an application) or mostly read them (a content site).
The fixed set of type sizes, each a step from the one before.
A sequence of sizes related by one ratio, such as 1.25. The ratios are named after musical intervals: minor second, major second, minor third, major third, perfect fourth.
terms.source: Tim Brown, More Meaningful Typography, A List Apart, 2011; modularscale.com (read 2026-11-11)

terms.meaning: The distance between baselines of consecutive lines. Typographers call it leading.
The uniform space added between characters. Typographers call it tracking.
The length of a line of running text, counted in characters.
The fixed set of distances, usually multiples of one base unit.
The corner treatment of surfaces and controls, set as a corner radius scale.
terms.source: Common practice (Material Design names the section Shape)

terms.meaning: How round a corner is. Material Design 3 names a scale of them: none 0, extra small 4, small 8, medium 12, large 16, and larger steps up to full.
A fixed vertical step that line heights and spacing snap to, so text on different parts of a page lines up. Material Design 1 uses 4dp for type and 8dp for components.
How far a surface sits above another, shown by shadow or tone.
The durations and easing curves of transitions, and when a transition is allowed.
How tightly controls and rows are packed, as a named setting rather than per-component sizes.
Columns, gutters and margins that place content, with breakpoints where the arrangement changes.
The icon set and its drawing rules: grid, keylines, stroke weight.
A deliberate departure from the computed value because the eye reads the computed one as wrong. Recorded with its reason.
terms.source: Common practice in type and icon design

terms.meaning: Components from the smallest to larger groups. A description of size, not a folder layout.
Page-level objects that place components in a layout and state the structure of the content.
Templates filled with real content.
The components and conventions shared by the whole organisation.
terms.source: Brad Frost, The art of design system recipes

terms.meaning: The components of the core design system: the shared, closed set every product builds from.
terms.source: The owner's architecture note of 2026-11-09, after Brad Frost's core design system

terms.meaning: Compositions specific to one product. Outside the core, still built on its tokens.
terms.source: Brad Frost, The art of design system recipes

terms.meaning: One-off pieces used in a single place. They need a reason and an expiry.
terms.source: Brad Frost, The art of design system recipes

terms.meaning: A recipe that has proved its worth moves into the core.
terms.source: Brad Frost, The art of design system recipes

terms.meaning: The named parts of a component.
One of a closed set of looks or purposes a component offers.
What a component or a view shows because of a condition: hover, focus, pressed, disabled, selected for a control; loading, empty, error for a view.
A named place in a component that takes content.
Components that supply behaviour and accessibility with no styling.
How to build accessibility semantics into a widget such as a dialog, a combobox or tabs. The guide calls them patterns.
terms.source: W3C, ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG), Patterns (read 2026-11-11)

terms.meaning: Repeatable answers to a recurring task: saving, notifying, waiting, failing, being empty, searching, filtering.

A list of items and the one item opened from it, arranged together: side by side where both fit, one at a time where they do not. A side sheet over the list and a page of its own are the other arrangements.
terms.source: Common practice (Material Design 3 names list-detail among its canonical layouts)

terms.meaning: What a view shows when there is nothing yet, with the first action to take.
What a view shows while content is on its way, usually a skeleton of the coming content.
What a view shows when a request failed, with what failed and how to retry.
An action that removes something and cannot be undone. It asks for confirmation and names the thing.
The rules for words: voice and tone, button labels, error sentences, formats.
Voice is the constant character of the writing; tone is how it shifts with the situation.
Adapting a product to the language, cultural and other requirements of a target market (a locale). It covers numeric, date and time formats and the use of currency, among other things.

The kind of data a table column holds, which decides its alignment and formatting: numbers right-aligned, text left-aligned. No single industry name exists; Polaris says column content types, MUI column types, AG Grid cell data types.
terms.source: Shopify Polaris, Data table; MUI X Data Grid, Column definition; AG Grid, Cell data types (read 2026-11-11)

terms.meaning: The channel that delivers component code: a JSON index where each item lists its files and dependencies, installed into the project by a command.
The machine-readable index of components: options, variants, defaults.
A real build chosen as the model to copy.
The opinionated, supported way. Leaving it is allowed and unsupported.
terms.source: Spotify Engineering, How we use Golden Paths

terms.meaning: Shape the types so that a wrong state cannot be written.
Static checks that reject values and structures outside the system.
Whether what was built matches what the system decided, and the checks that show it.
terms.source: Common practice (the owner's architecture note of 2026-11-09 uses it as a cross-cutting layer)

terms.meaning: How the system reaches the repositories that use it: a registry for code, a plugin for checks and procedures.
terms.source: Common practice (the owner's architecture note of 2026-11-09 uses it as a cross-cutting layer)

terms.meaning: A review of what exists against what the system says, ending in a list of gaps.
Comparing rendered screens against approved images.
Who may change the system, how changes are reviewed, and how adoption is tracked. Includes the contribution model.
The share of the product built from the system's components, and the count of detached variants.
A short page that states one decision, its context and its consequences.
Shared test tools: test templates, readiness waits, break-it checks.
Five rungs for how firmly a decision is held, from cannot-be-written-wrong down to written guidance, plus design judgment.
Decisions with an automated check that can fail, divided by all decisions.

One of the moments in a repository's life at which the plugin acts: the repository is born, it meets the plugin, a feature needs a new block, every change, and periodically before handing over. Status gives one line for each.
terms.source: The owner's architecture document for the meta layer, section on the life of a repository, 2026-11-13

terms.meaning: The record, kept in the repository, of which version of the plugin its copy of the tool came from and the hash git gives that folder. What a lockfile is to a dependency.
terms.source: The specification of the command set, 2026-11-15
